issues.description: validate_conda uses substring match that accepts any path containing 'conda' or 'mamba'
issues.detail: The check `any(tool in out.decode().lower() for tool in ["micromamba", "mamba", "conda"])` runs on the entire `--version` stdout. A binary that prints anything containing those substrings passes. Worse, the data structure is wrong here: `--version` output is well-shaped (`conda 24.5.0`), so parse it as `tool version` and check the first token. The algorithm follows from the data once you pick the right shape.

issues.description: validate_conda ignores stderr and the process return code
issues.detail: run_program(...).communicate() returns (stdout, stderr) and the function discards stderr with `__`, then never checks returncode. Some conda-like tools print version to stderr; a non-zero exit is silently treated as success if stdout happens to contain the substring. Check returncode == 0 and look at both streams, or just use subprocess.run with check.

issues.description: filters='*.exe' on the file picker is Windows-only and will hide valid executables on macOS/Linux
issues.detail: Conda/mamba/micromamba on Unix have no extension. A `*.exe` filter on the QFileDialog will make the browse dialog show nothing useful for the majority of conda installations. Either drop the filter or branch on platform. Small data point, big UX consequence.

issues.description: Empty string treated as 'valid' is a quiet convention worth a comment or rename
issues.detail: `validate_conda("")` returns True so the field validates while empty. That's fine, but the function name promises validation of an executable; the empty-string shortcut is a UI concern leaking into a utility. A one-line comment explaining 'empty means unset, validated elsewhere' would prevent future confusion.

issues.description: Fallback logic in argv() reads cleaner as a small helper
issues.detail: The nested `self.get_conf(...) if self.get_conf(...) else None` pattern bundles two concerns: 'is the custom override enabled' and 'what is its value'. A two-line helper `_custom_conda_override()` returning the path or None makes the call site read as a single line and isolates the config lookup. Small filter shape; algorithm becomes obvious.

issues.description: setFocus() side effect added to a generic helper used by all browsefile callers
issues.detail: `select_file` now calls `edit.setFocus()` after any browsefile selection across the codebase. That's a behavior change for every consumer of `create_browsefile`, not just the new conda field. If focus-on-validate is what's wanted, wire it at the call site or via a flag; don't mutate shared infrastructure for one caller's benefit.

review.summary: The feature is small and the data flow is right: a checkbox plus a path, consulted as a fallback in one place. Most of the code earns its keep. The weak spot is the validator: it's doing substring matching on free-form output and ignoring both stderr and exit code, which is exactly the kind of cleverness that gets fooled by an unrelated binary whose help text mentions 'conda'. Parse the `tool version` shape and the algorithm is one line. Also: `*.exe` filter is Windows-only and will silently hide valid executables on Unix, and adding `setFocus()` to the shared `select_file` helper is a side effect that doesn't belong to this PR. Nothing here is structural — strip the cleverness in the validator and the rest is fine.
